title: Search in Rotated Sorted Array II
summary: Given an integer array sorted in non-decreasing order and rotated at an unknown pivot, determine if a target integer is present.
statement: Given an integer array sorted in non-decreasing order and rotated at an unknown pivot, determine if a target integer is present. Return true if the target is found, otherwise false. Minimize the number of operations.
constraints: 1–5000 integers, each between -10000 and 10000; target is in the same numeric range.
nums is a rotation of a nondecreasing array and may contain duplicates. Return a Boolean, not an index.
Discard a sorted half when comparisons determine it; equal boundary/middle values may require shrinking the search interval one step.
target_time_complexity: O(log n) when halves are distinguishable; O(n) worst case with duplicates
hints: One side is normally sorted, but duplicates can hide which side contains the rotation.
Check the middle first. If left, middle, and right are equal, remove the two checked boundary values.
Otherwise identify a sorted half, test whether its value interval includes the target, and keep only the relevant half.
Do not promise worst-case logarithmic time: many equal values can force linear shrinking.
editorial: Binary search normally identifies one sorted half from boundary and middle comparisons. If both boundaries equal the middle and the middle is not the target, both boundaries can be safely removed, but no entire half is justified. Otherwise use the sorted half's inclusive/exclusive value interval to choose the next search range. An interval with one element must still be checked. The independent oracle uses direct membership rather than interval elimination.

tests.explanation: Zero occurs twice, so return True regardless of which matching position is found.
Neither sorted portion contains 3, so return False.
